business_problem: Paylocity's Community collaboration platform was growing faster than expected, and its previous database became rigid, expensive, slow, and operationally heavy as user and content volumes increased.
solution_summary: Paylocity migrated its Community employee-collaboration platform onto MongoDB Atlas on AWS to replace a rigid incumbent database with a fully managed document store. Because the original platform already used a MongoDB API, the team could reuse much of its existing code, build a five-node Atlas deployment, and add a feature-flag system that switched traffic between the old and new databases during the cutover. Atlas stores Community posts, attachments, comments, and company content for millions of active users while reducing maintenance work for the engineering team. Atlas dashboards and MongoDB Atlas Charts provide monitoring, alerts, analytics, and visualizations so engineers can study query behavior and tune performance over time. That architecture delivered faster response times without changing the product model for users, and it gave Paylocity the operational visibility needed to forecast growth and keep the collaboration experience responsive as adoption continued to climb.
